instructions:
Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 183 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

A measurement tool scored the draft on how it carries feeling. For each measure below it gives the current value and a target. Revise the essay so that its measures move to the targets; the tool will score the result again.
- positive charge (hedons per 1,000 words): now 91.2, target 64.8. Counts positive words such as good, love, fun.
- negative charge (dolors per 1,000 words): now 6.5, target 4.1. Counts negative words such as bad, hate, problem.
- words that carry charge (% of words): now 27.3, target 16.4. Counts share of all words that carry any feeling.
- charge under a negation (% of charge): now 4.4, target 6.6. Counts feeling words placed under not, never or n't.
- charge after an intensifier such as 'very' (% of charge): now 0.0, target 1.4. Counts feeling words placed right after very, really or so.
- charge after a contrast word such as 'but' (% of charge): now 3.7, target 24.2. Counts feeling words placed after but or however in the same sentence.
- net charge of the last fifth minus the text's mean (per 1,000 words): now 20.6, target -6.0. Counts how much more positive the last fifth is than the essay as a whole; negative means a more downbeat ending.
- how unevenly charge is spread over sentences (1 = as if words were dealt at random): now 1.4, target 1.0. Counts above 1 means the feeling is bunched into some sentences while others are plain; below 1 means it is spread evenly.

Draft:

Dear Principal,

I think our school should require every student to do some community service, as long as the number of hours stays reasonable.

Some of my friends tutor second graders at Lincoln Elementary after school. At first they went only because a teacher asked them to. Now they talk about "their kids" all the time, and one of them wants to become a teacher. She would never have found that out if nobody had pushed her to try.

Other friends spent a Saturday picking up litter along the creek behind the park. They filled twenty bags, and the next week people were walking their dogs there again. A few hours of work changed the place for the whole neighborhood.

I know some students worry that service will take time away from homework, sports, or jobs. That is a fair concern. But a requirement of ten or fifteen hours a year, with many choices of when and where to serve, would not overload anyone.

Required service teaches responsibility and helps our town. Please make it part of our school.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
